title: Older Ages for 23 Pre-main Sequence Stars in Upper Scorpius Using Dynamical-mass-constrained Stellar Evolutionary Models
question: Derive revised stellar ages for 23 pre-main sequence K- and M-type stars in Upper Scorpius by using CO-derived stellar dynamical masses to constrain isochronal ages from five pre-main sequence stellar evolutionary models.

recipe.goal: Obtain stellar dynamical masses from ALMA CO J=3-2 disk kinematics
recipe.method: Model Keplerian disk rotation in ALMA CO J=3-2 line data combined with Gaia distances using MCMC fitting (performed in Towner et al. 2025).

recipe.goal: Derive unconstrained isochronal masses and ages
recipe.method: Generate 10,000-point Gaussian distributions in T_eff and L_bol for each source, linearly interpolate onto five PMS evolutionary track grids (BHAC15, PARSEC v1.1, PARSEC v1.2S, Feiden 2016 non-magnetic and magnetic), and compute median and 1.4826*MAD of the resulting mass and age distributions.
key_parameters: 10,000 points per Gaussian distribution in T_eff and L_bol
Track points restricted to within 3 sigma
assumptions: Gaussian error distributions for T_eff and L_bol
For a normal distribution, 1.4826 x MAD is equivalent to 1 sigma

recipe.goal: Derive dynamical-mass-constrained isochronal ages and summary statistics
recipe.method: Filter the (M_*, tau) pairs from each PMS track to retain only those where isochronal M_* agrees with dynamical mass within uncertainties, then compute median tau, scaled MAD, age ratios (tau_all/tau_dyn), absolute age changes (Delta tau), and intra-source age spreads (sigma_tau).
key_parameters: Sample restricted to sources with both unconstrained and mass-constrained ages (automatically M_dyn <= 1 M_sun)

recipe.goal: Test for linear and non-linear correlations between stellar mass, age, and model accuracy
recipe.method: Calculate Spearman's rho correlation coefficients and p-values between dynamical mass, mass-constrained age, isochronal-to-dynamical mass ratio, and unconstrained-to-constrained age ratio across all five model sets, and visually inspect scatterplots for non-linear trends.

recipe.goal: Test for age bias in the 23-star sample against the broader Upper Sco K- and M-type population
recipe.method: Select Upper Sco K- and M-type stars from Fang & Herczeg (2025) using Luhman (2022) and Ratzenböck et al. (2023a) kinematic group criteria, compute their Feiden (2016) magnetic isochronal ages and masses, and perform 2-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Anderson-Darling tests against the 23-star sample.
key_parameters: Luhman (2022) kinematic groups u, ul, ulc, uc (2059 K- and M-type sources)
Ratzenböck et al. (2023a) SigMA groups 1 through 9 inclusive (2469 K- and M-type sources)

score_reason: The core analysis in this paper (Monte Carlo interpolation of T_eff, L_bol, and M_dyn onto five public PMS evolutionary tracks) is fully tabular, with all input stellar properties provided in Table 1 and output ages in Table 2. Minor ambiguities remain regarding the exact treatment of asymmetric error bars in Table 1 and 2D track interpolation details, while the upstream ALMA CO dynamical mass fitting is entirely deferred to Towner et al. (2025).
rediscovery_reason: All input parameters (M_dyn, L_bol, T_eff, distances) for the 23 stars are explicitly tabulated in Table 1, the five PMS evolutionary track grids are standard public datasets, the Monte Carlo filtering recipe is simple and self-contained, and the main results (Tables 2, 3, 4) are cleanly numeric.
